verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,
“This month shall be to you the beginning of months. It shall be the first month of the year to you.
Speak to all the congregation of Israel, saying, ‘On the tenth day of this month, they shall take to them every man a lamb, according to their fathers’ houses, a lamb for a household;

and if the household is too little for a lamb, then he and his neighbor next to his house shall take one according to the number of the souls; according to what everyone can eat you shall make your count for the lamb.
Your lamb shall be without defect, a male a year old. You shall take it from the sheep, or from the goats:
and you shall keep it until the fourteenth day of the same month; and the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall kill it at evening.
They shall take some of the blood, and put it on the two door posts and on the lintel, on the houses in which they shall eat it.
They shall eat the meat in that night, roasted with fire, and unleavened bread. They shall eat it with bitter herbs.
Don’t eat it raw, nor boiled at all with water, but roasted with fire; with its head, its legs and its inner parts.
You shall let nothing of it remain until the morning; but that which remains of it until the morning you shall burn with fire.
This is how you shall eat it: with your belt on your waist, your shoes on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and you shall eat it in haste: it is Yahweh’s Passover.

For I will go through the land of Egypt in that night, and will strike all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both man and animal. Against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgments: I am Yahweh.
The blood shall be to you for a token on the houses where you are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and there shall no plague be on you to destroy you, when I strike the land of Egypt.
This day shall be to you for a memorial, and you shall keep it a feast to Yahweh: throughout your generations you shall keep it a feast by an ordinance forever.

“‘Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread; even the first day you shall put away yeast out of your houses, for whoever eats leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Israel.

In the first day there shall be to you a holy convocation, and in the seventh day a holy convocation; no kind of work shall be done in them, except that which every man must eat, that only may be done by you.

You shall observe the feast of unleavened bread; for in this same day I have brought your armies out of the land of Egypt: therefore you shall observe this day throughout your generations by an ordinance forever.
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at evening, you shall eat unleavened bread, until the twenty first day of the month at evening.

There shall be no yeast found in your houses for seven days, for whoever eats that which is leavened, that soul shall be cut off from the congregation of Israel, whether he is a foreigner, or one who is born in the land.
You shall eat nothing leavened. In all your habitations you shall eat unleavened bread.’”
Then Moses called for all the elders of Israel, and said to them, “Draw out, and take lambs according to your families, and kill the Passover.

You shall take a bunch of hyssop, and dip it in the blood that is in the basin, and strike the lintel and the two door posts with the blood that is in the basin; and none of you shall go out of the door of his house until the morning.

For Yahweh will pass through to strike the Egyptians; and when he sees the blood on the lintel, and on the two door posts, Yahweh will pass over the door, and will not allow the destroyer to come in to your houses to strike you.
You shall observe this thing for an ordinance to you and to your sons forever.
It shall happen when you have come to the land which Yahweh will give you, according as he has promised, that you shall keep this service.
It will happen, when your children ask you, ‘What do you mean by this service?’

that you shall say, ‘It is the sacrifice of Yahweh’s Passover, who passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt, when he struck the Egyptians, and spared our houses.’” The people bowed their heads and worshiped.
The children of Israel went and did so; as Yahweh had commanded Moses and Aaron, so they did.

At midnight, Yahweh struck all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sat on his throne to the firstborn of the captive who was in the dungeon; and all the firstborn of livestock.
Pharaoh rose up in the night, he, and all his servants, and all the Egyptians; and there was a great cry in Egypt, for there was not a house where there was not one dead.
He called for Moses and Aaron by night, and said, “Rise up, get out from among my people, both you and the children of Israel; and go, serve Yahweh, as you have said!
Take both your flocks and your herds, as you have said, and be gone; and bless me also!”
The Egyptians were urgent with the people, to send them out of the land in haste, for they said, “We are all dead men.”
The people took their dough before it was leavened, their kneading troughs being bound up in their clothes on their shoulders.
The children of Israel did according to the word of Moses; and they asked of the Egyptians jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and clothing.
Yahweh gave the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they let them have what they asked. They plundered the Egyptians.
The children of Israel traveled from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot who were men, besides children.
A mixed multitude went up also with them, with flocks, herds, and even very much livestock.

They baked unleavened cakes of the dough which they brought out of Egypt; for it wasn’t leavened, because they were thrust out of Egypt, and couldn’t wait, and they had not prepared any food for themselves.
Now the time that the children of Israel lived in Egypt was four hundred thirty years.
At the end of four hundred thirty years, to the day, all of Yahweh’s armies went out from the land of Egypt.
It is a night to be much observed to Yahweh for bringing them out from the land of Egypt. This is that night of Yahweh, to be much observed of all the children of Israel throughout their generations.
Yahweh said to Moses and Aaron, “This is the ordinance of the Passover. No foreigner shall eat of it,
but every man’s servant who is bought for money, when you have circumcised him, then shall he eat of it.
A foreigner and a hired servant shall not eat of it.
It must be eaten In one house. You shall not carry any of the meat outside of the house. Do not break any of its bones.
All the congregation of Israel shall keep it.

When a stranger shall live as a foreigner with you, and will keep the Passover to Yahweh, let all his males be circumcised, and then let him come near and keep it; and he shall be as one who is born in the land: but no uncircumcised person shall eat of it.
One law shall be to him who is born at home, and to the stranger who lives as a foreigner among you.”
All the children of Israel did so. As Yahweh commanded Moses and Aaron, so they did.
That same day, Yahweh brought the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt by their armies.

footnotes.content: The Lord speaks now. When God draws near to say something with His own mouth, everything pivots. Moses and Aaron listen—and so the whole story turns. What a mercy, that He speaks at all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A new calendar begins. Not by human will, but by God's sovereign word. When grace saves you, the old way of counting time ends. Every day after deliverance is numbered from the fact of His rescue.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Every household, down to the smallest family, takes a lamb. The Lord sees each one—He forgets no one. Redemption isn't a mass event; it's personal and particular. He counts every soul.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even if a household is too small, neighbors share the lamb. Grace binds us together. No one is left to face the coming judgment alone—the Lord designs it so we stand with one another.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The lamb must be without defect. Blemished won't do. A shadow falls here—redemption costs the precious and the perfect. Long centuries later, we meet the Lamb who bore no flaw.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Four days the lamb is kept, watched. Then at evening—the assembly kills it. Even here, the act is shared, witnessed, not hidden. The people see what their deliverance costs.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Blood on the doorposts and lintel. A sign He reads, not the angel. The destroyer sees the blood and passes by. Our salvation rests not on what we see or understand, but on what the Lord sees.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Roasted meat, bitter herbs, bread without leaven. Haste in the eating, urgency in the meal. They taste the sorrow of slavery even as they taste deliverance. Redemption is not forgetting—it's remembering.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Not raw, not boiled—only roasted with fire. The lamb is wholly consumed, wholly transformed. In His fire, the work is complete. No half measures in redemption.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Nothing remains until morning; what's left is burned. The Lord hates waste—and hates the idea that His grace might be hoarded or doubted. Each day receives its portion fresh.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Belt on, shoes on, staff in hand. The posture of readiness, of journeying. This is Yahweh's Passover—the moment of rescue. It calls us to wake, to watch, to be ready for what He is doing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Midnight comes. The Lord passes through Egypt, and judgment falls on every house—man, animal, god alike. Egypt's idols are exposed as nothing. His power alone stands.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When I see the blood, I will pass over you. The blood is a token—a sign the Lord reads. He passes over His people not because He doesn't see them, but because He sees them marked with the blood of the lamb.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A memorial forever—not so Israel forgets, but so they never forget. Each year the feast says: He passed over us. He chose us. He saved us. Memory keeps hope alive.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Seven days without leaven. Yeast is old, dead matter that rises with air. The Lord calls His people away from the old, swollen, hollow ways—to the new and simple. He cleanses as He saves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Holy convocations, no work save eating. The Lord calls the people to set apart, to gather, to rest in what He has done. Work ceases because the work is His.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: This same day—no delay, no wandering. The Lord brings out His armies at the exact moment of promise. His word and His work are not divided; He speaks and it stands.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Evening of the fourteenth until evening of the twenty-first—time marked, contained, held. The feast anchors the people in a precise frame. God loves order, clarity, boundaries.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No leaven in the houses, for native or foreigner alike. The same law binds all who stand with the Lord's people. Grace doesn't lower its standard; it raises all to the same high ground.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Only unleavened bread in your homes. A simple rule, repeated—yet it speaks volumes. The Lord wants His redeemed people to see, taste, and remember: the old way is gone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses calls the elders. Leadership passes down the word. The people don't hear it as a rumor; they hear it as command through those who shepherd them. Truth travels by voice.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hyssop—a lowly plant, yet chosen for the great work. The destroyer will pass over. Even the humblest instrument, dipped in blood and faith, becomes part of redemption's sign.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The destroyer sees the blood and passes by. There's no bargaining with death, no hiding—only the mark of the sacrifice. Those who hide behind the blood live; those who don't, don't.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Forever, an ordinance. God doesn't give laws that expire. What He institutes for His people stands as long as His people stand. The Passover is ancient now, yet alive in every generation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When you come to the land—the promise looks ahead. Deliverance from Egypt is real, but it isn't the end. The Lord is already moving them toward the inheritance He swore to give.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Your children will ask. The Lord builds in the question. He knows children come with eyes open, wanting to know the why and the how. He honors the searching heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Tell them: it is the Lord's Passover—He passed over us, struck the Egyptians, spared our houses. The people bow and worship. How right that remembering His mercy draws us to our knees.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They obeyed. What the Lord commanded through Moses and Aaron, the people did. Not perfect obedience, not later, but prompt and complete. The redeemed respond to the Redeemer.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: At midnight—the Lord strikes. Pharaoh's son, captive, firstborn of cattle—all fall. No partiality in judgment. What stands outside the blood falls to the sword.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Great cry in Egypt. Not a whisper, not a debate—a wail. The night of deliverance is the night of reckoning. For those who reject God's mercy, His power becomes their undoing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Pharaoh calls by night—no daylight, no witnesses he can hide from, just the dark and the loss. He begs Moses: go, take your people, serve your God. Even hardened hearts break under God's hand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bless me also. Pharaoh, who said 'Who is Yahweh?', now begs a blessing from Moses' God. How the proud learn humility when the Lord moves in judgment and grace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Egyptians urge them out in haste—they fear for their own lives. The oppressors become the ones who drive their slaves to freedom. The Lord turns all things to His purpose.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Their dough not yet leavened—they depart so suddenly there's no time for bread to rise. The rush echoes still: when the Lord calls, we don't delay to perfect our preparations.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They asked of the Egyptians—gold, silver, clothing. The Lord gives His people favor; the oppressors give willingly what they once withheld. What was stolen in labor is restored in honor.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord gave them favor. His power moves in mercy too—not just in judgment. The Egyptians' own hearts bend toward kindness when the Lord inclines them so.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Six hundred thousand men on foot—a nation born in the wilderness. The Lord multiplies what He treasures. When He saves, He saves not a handful but peoples, armies, multitudes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A mixed multitude went with them—foreigners, flocks, herds. The Lord's deliverance spreads beyond Israel's borders. Those who walk with His people share in His mercy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Unleavened cakes from dough brought out unready—no time to leaven, no time to prepare. They eat what they can make in haste. Sometimes obedience means moving before we're ready.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Four hundred thirty years in Egypt—a long slavery, measured in generations. The Lord doesn't forget even the longest night. His patience holds fast until the hour He has set.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: To the day—the very day He promised. God's word is never late, never uncertain. Precision marks His faithfulness. The wait ends exactly when He said.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A night to be much observed—made holy by what the Lord did. We don't observe nights by accident or habit; we observe them in wonder at His works. This night changed everything.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The ordinance of the Passover: no foreigner eats of it. A boundary is set—not from cruelty, but to mark what is sacred. Some things are reserved for those who belong to the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A servant bought for money, once circumcised, may eat. The way in isn't bloodline alone—it's covenant. Even a slave, marked by the sign of the covenant, becomes part of the household.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A foreigner and hired servant shall not eat of it. Not all are called to this table. The line between insider and outsider exists by God's design, though His design always holds possibility for crossing it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: One house, the meat not carried out, no bones broken—wholeness, unity, a single dwelling. These details speak of the Lamb later: His body dwelt in one temple, unbroken, whole.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All the congregation shall keep it. No exemptions, no excuses. Every soul the Lord has redeemed is called to remember and feast. His salvation binds all into one family.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A foreigner living among them may keep the Passover if circumcised. The door stands open to those who choose the covenant. The Lord's grace reaches to the stranger who says yes to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: One law for the native and the foreigner. The Lord doesn't lower His standard for outsiders or raise it to keep them out—one law, one call, one grace for all who belong to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All the children of Israel did so. Again, obedience. The people hear the command and do it. Faith answers and moves. That's how a nation becomes one redeemed people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in this verse—not just the Exodus, but the echoing call to arise and follow. The Lord brought Israel out by their armies; He invites us still into His grand procession of redeemed. As of 2026-10, that call remains open.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
